name: Ewondo
notes: Ewondo (Beti, Kolo), Bantu A.72 of the Beti-Fang cluster, spoken in the forests south of the Sanaga river across the Centre, East and Littoral regions of Cameroon, historically the Beti people's lingua franca and a former colonial mission/school language. Latin orthography harmonised in the 1970s under the General Alphabet of Cameroon Languages, with the African-reference-alphabet vowel letters ə ɛ ɔ. Eight vowels /i e ɛ ə a ɔ o u/. Consonant inventory includes voiceless/voiced plosives p b t d k g, the labial-velars kp/gb, their prenasalised counterparts mb/nd/ng/ngb, the affricates ts/dz and prenasalised ndz, and a prenasalised labiodental fricative vy=/ᶬv/ distinct from plain v; ny=/ɲ/. Seven contrastive tones are reported (Essono 1978's dissertation on Ewondo phonology-morphology-syntax; Wikipedia's Ewondo language phonology section): high (acute), mid-high (grave), mid (macron), low/mid-low (unmarked, the default), rising (caron) and falling (circumflex) are all attested as written diacritics on vowels in careful orthography, though ordinary text often leaves tone unmarked (as for related Duala/Basaa in this dataset).
